In January 2018,[Ozempic](https://www.phoenix.ca/medications/ozempic) , a GLP-1 receptor agonist with the active ingredient semaglutide, was[approved by Health Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-product-database.html) and became available in Canada with a prescription.


GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) is a hormone your body naturally releases after eating. Prescription treatments in this class work by mimicking this hormone. They signal the brain that you're full, slow the rate at which the stomach empties, and help regulate blood sugar levels. These biological effects make them a prescription treatment option that licensed healthcare providers evaluate on a case-by-case basis.


Getting an Ozempic prescription in Canada, though, hasn't always been straightforward. Supply shortages, long wait times, and limited access to family doctors have all created hurdles for men looking to connect with a licensed healthcare provider.


**TLDR:**


- Canadian patients face an average wait of 30 weeks from GP referral to specialist, per a 2024 Fraser Institute study.
- You may be eligible for a GLP-1 prescription with a BMI of 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with a weight-related condition.
- Men's telehealth clinics let you complete a health assessment online and receive your prescription in discreet packaging.
- Five Health Canada approved GLP-1 class prescription options are available in Canada, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound.
- Phoenix connects Canadian men with licensed healthcare providers for online weight management prescription assessments.


## Barriers to Getting Ozempic in Canada


From August 2023 to March 2024, Canada experienced significant[Ozempic shortages](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-shortages.html) due to increased worldwide demand for the medication. The surge in demand was largely driven by social media, particularly content about the health journeys of Hollywood icons, and off-label use. Healthcare professionals recommended increasing the supply to the manufacturer, and production was ramped up to meet the demand by the spring of 2024.


Now that the demand for Ozempic has been met, the only remaining roadblock to men seeking Ozempic in Canada comes from the healthcare system itself.


According to a[2024 study from the Fraser Institute](https://www.fraserinstitute.org/studies/waiting-your-turn-wait-times-for-health-care-in-canada-2024) , Canadian patients faced an average wait time of 30 weeks from a general practitioner referral to seeing a specialist, a significant increase from previous years. Finding a family doctor can also be challenging, with many people waiting months or even years to find a practitioner. On top of that, only 26% of Canadians got same-day or next-day appointments, as of 2023, according to the Canadian Medical Association.


Cost is another practical consideration. In most Canadian provinces, GLP-1 prescription treatments for weight management are not covered by provincial health insurance plans, which means most men pay out of pocket. Private insurance plans vary widely in what they cover, and coverage often depends on the approved indication and individual plan terms. Checking with your insurer before starting treatment can help you understand what, if any, reimbursement is available. Men's online health clinics typically publish their pricing upfront, so you can review costs before committing to an assessment.


With healthcare wait times increasing and access to experts decreasing, the way men receive care in Canada needed to change. That's where men's telehealth services bridge the gap and make a big difference.


## Who May Be Eligible for an Ozempic Prescription in Canada


A licensed Canadian healthcare provider reviews each patient individually. While eligibility is always determined on a case-by-case basis, providers typically consider the following factors during a medical assessment:


- **Body mass index (BMI):** A BMI of 30 or higher, or a BMI of 27 or higher with at least one weight-related health condition such as high blood pressure or type 2 diabetes
- **Health history:** No personal or family history of certain thyroid conditions (such as medullary thyroid carcinoma), pancreatitis, or other conditions that may make GLP-1 treatments unsuitable
- **Current medications:** A provider will check for interactions with other prescription treatments you may already be taking
- **Age:** GLP-1 prescription treatments are generally prescribed to adults; your provider will confirm whether the treatment is appropriate for your age group
- **Weight management goals:** Providers look at whether a prescription plan aligns with your longer-term health goals and whether lifestyle changes alone have not been sufficient


If you meet these general criteria, a telehealth assessment is the fastest way to connect with a licensed Canadian provider and find out whether a prescription is right for you. Your provider may also ask about your lifestyle, activity level, and previous weight management approaches to build a full picture of your health before making a determination.

## Possible Side Effects and Safety Considerations


GLP-1 receptor agonists and GIP/GLP-1 dual agonists are prescription medications, and like all prescription treatments they come with possible side effects. A licensed healthcare provider will review your health history before prescribing and can help you weigh the potential benefits against the risks.


Commonly reported side effects include:


- Nausea
- Vomiting
- Diarrhea
- Constipation
- Stomach discomfort or bloating


These effects are often mild and tend to occur early in treatment. More serious reactions are less common but possible. For a detailed breakdown of what to expect, see our[GLP-1 side effects week-by-week guide](https://www.phoenix.ca/blog/glp1-semaglutide-side-effects-week-week) . Your provider will discuss the full safety profile with you during your assessment and can answer any questions about interactions with other medications you may be taking.


These medications are not appropriate for everyone. People with a personal or family history of certain thyroid conditions, pancreatitis, or other specific health concerns may not be eligible. A thorough medical screening helps identify whether a prescription is suitable for you.
